Not really, the surge of posts in /v/aww came in response to an obnoxious troll who kept posting gore. People wanted to drown out the horrible stuff with better content that actually fit the subverse. That wasn't ever really necessary though, since all the troll posts got downvoated to hell and very few people ever even saw them - the system worked as intended. But the people posting the cute stuff kept going anyway, to the point where they started getting a significant backlash - one even worse than the response to the initial troll posting, amusingly. Seems that some people around here saw it as spam, or forum sliding like you mention, or account farming, or some other kind of nefarious or suspicious activity. And a few ran into a quirk of voat where they couldn't block the subverse and that pissed them off (if you don't subscribe to any subverses, it substitutes in the default set which includes aww, and you can't block any of your subscribed subs).

But forum sliding doesn't work on voat. Everyone gets their own custom tailored view of posts, where they can choose their own selection of subverses, or they can filter out any particular ones they don't want when they view /v/all. A flood of posts in one subverse doesn't necessarily mean that other posts get pushed off the front page. Even for the people who don't block anything and view the defaults or /v/all, the system still worked as intended and the flood of cute posts started getting regularly downvoated after the backlash started, so they didn't really affect a whole lot for very many people or for very long.

The ones who started flooding posts in aww were probably just normal people who happen to like cute little animals and aww-worthy content, and who saw the trolling and wanted to do something to fight back against a real problem that affected them and a place they liked. It probably got some lurkers who wouldn't normally post to come out of hiding and participate. But I can't say that there was ever any kind of organization behind it or that any of them were bots - it's certainly possible, but the way I see it makes sense to me and seems a lot more plausible. I just haven't seen any evidence to suggest otherwise.
